questions.question: A Boolean minimizer drops the product term q∧r from (p∧q)∨(¬p∧r)∨(q∧r) because every assignment satisfying q∧r already satisfies one of the other two terms. Which theorem justifies deleting it?
alternatives: the consensus theorem for Boolean terms
questions.explanation: By the consensus theorem (p∧q)∨(¬p∧r)∨(q∧r) ≡ (p∧q)∨(¬p∧r): the consensus term q∧r is absorbed because its rows are covered by whichever of p or ¬p holds.

questions.question: A verification engineer models ∧, ∨, ¬ as meet, join, and complement on a set, and checks commutativity, associativity, distributivity, identity, and complement laws before doing algebra on formulas. Which algebraic structure has she shown the operations form?
questions.explanation: A Boolean algebra is a complemented distributive lattice — exactly the algebraic structure formalizing ∧, ∨, ¬ with those laws.

questions.question: To certify a structure as a Boolean algebra, a formalization checks a short list: commutativity and associativity of both operations, distributivity, identity elements, and complementation — the minimal axiom set published by Edward Huntington in 1904. Whose axiomatization is this?
questions.explanation: Huntington's axiomatization defines Boolean algebras via a small set of equational axioms on two binary operations plus complementation.

questions.question: A logician represents each element of a Boolean algebra by the set of ultrafilters containing it, turning ∧, ∨, ¬ into ∩, ∪, and complement — embedding the algebra into a power-set algebra. Which theorem guarantees every Boolean algebra admits such a representation?
alternatives: representation as a field of sets
questions.explanation: The Stone representation theorem states every Boolean algebra is isomorphic to a field of sets, so ∩, ∪, complement can always play the roles of ∧, ∨, ¬.

questions.question: A proof establishes the absorption identity p∧(p∨q) ≡ p. A student claims p∨(p∧q) ≡ p then follows with no additional work. Which principle — swap each connective and constant — justifies the claim?
questions.explanation: Duality: any Boolean identity stays valid after swapping ∧ with ∨ and False with True, so the dual absorption law comes free.

questions.question: A semantics needs truth values forming a Boolean algebra in which every subset — even infinite ones — has a join and a meet, so quantifiers over infinite domains stay well-defined. What is such an algebra called?
questions.explanation: A complete Boolean algebra has suprema and infima for every subset, not merely finite ones.

questions.question: A formula negates a whole set-indexed disjunction: ¬(⋁ᵢ pᵢ). Push the negation through the (possibly infinite) disjunction. What results?
questions.explanation: Generalized De Morgan: the negation of an arbitrary disjunction is the conjunction of the negations, ¬(⋁ᵢ pᵢ) ≡ ⋀ᵢ ¬pᵢ.

questions.question: A circuit synthesizer pins down one input of a Boolean function by splitting it into two cases: f(x) = (x∧f(1)) ∨ (¬x∧f(0)). Which expansion theorem is being applied?
questions.explanation: The Shannon (Boole) expansion writes f(x) ≡ (x∧f(1))∨(¬x∧f(0)), decomposing a function by the two possible values of one variable.

questions.question: A semantics is stipulated so that every proposition receives exactly one of two truth values — no truth-value gaps and no gluts. Which principle does this stipulation embody?
questions.explanation: Bivalence asserts every proposition is either true or false — the semantic underpinning of classical two-valued logic.

questions.question: A construction takes all formulas of a logic, groups them into classes modulo provable equivalence, and orders the classes by provable implication, obtaining a Boolean algebra. What is this algebra called?
questions.explanation: The Lindenbaum(-Tarski) algebra is the algebra of formulas quotiented by logical equivalence, ordered by provable implication.

questions.question: The formula (p∧¬q)∨(¬p∧r)∨(q∧¬r) is a disjunction in which every disjunct conjoins only literals. Which normal form is it already written in?
questions.explanation: A disjunction of conjunctions of literals is exactly disjunctive normal form.

questions.question: A SAT solver rejects (p∧q)∨r and demands input shaped like (p∨r)∧(q∨r): a conjunction of disjunctions of literals. Which normal form must the formula be converted into?
questions.explanation: Conjunctive normal form is a conjunction of clauses (disjunctions of literals), the standard SAT input; distributing ∨ over ∧ turns (p∧q)∨r into (p∨r)∧(q∨r).

questions.question: A chip library stocks only NAND gates, yet an engineer still builds NOT, AND, and OR subcircuits and thereby realizes any truth table. Which property of NAND makes the whole library sufficient?
questions.explanation: NAND alone is functionally complete: ¬p ≡ p↑p, p∧q ≡ (p↑q)↑(p↑q), and p∨q ≡ (p↑p)↑(q↑q), so every Boolean function is realizable.

questions.question: Analyzing a stream cipher, a cryptographer writes a Boolean function over GF(2) as f = p ⊕ q ⊕ (p∧q): an XOR of AND-monomials with no negations. Which normal form is this?
questions.explanation: Algebraic normal form (Reed-Muller/Zhegalkin polynomial) expresses a Boolean function as an XOR of conjunctions of variables over GF(2).

questions.question: A voting circuit must output 1 exactly when at least two of its three inputs p, q, r are 1. Construct the minimal DNF computing this majority function.
questions.explanation: At least two inputs high means one of the three pairs is fully high: (p∧q)∨(p∧r)∨(q∧r). Each pair-term is essential — drop one and the case where exactly that pair is high fails.

questions.question: Apply De Morgan's law twice to push the outer negation fully inward: ¬(p∨(¬q∧r)).
questions.explanation: First ¬(p∨X) = ¬p∧¬X; then ¬(¬q∧r) = q∨¬r, giving ¬p∧(q∨¬r).

questions.question: Simplify (p∧q)∨(¬p∧q)∨(p∧¬q)∨(¬p∧¬q) — the disjunction of all four minterms over p and q.
questions.explanation: The four minterms cover every truth assignment, so the disjunction is a tautology.

questions.question: A compiler simplifies !(a && (b || !c)). Push the negation fully inward using De Morgan's laws.
alternatives: not a or (not b and c)

questions.question: Using distribution and complementation, simplify (p∨q)∧(¬p∨q)∧p to its smallest equivalent.
questions.explanation: (p∨q)∧(¬p∨q) = q∨(p∧¬p) = q∨False = q; then q∧p = p∧q.

questions.question: Simplify p∨(¬p∧q) to a two-literal disjunction.
questions.explanation: Distribute: (p∨¬p)∧(p∨q) = True∧(p∨q) = p∨q — the absorption-like 'reduction' identity.
